gap_as_briefed: The simulated mount is never in a 'slewing' state -- a slew completes instantly.
gap_verdict: PARTLY ALREADY FIXED. The timed-slew model already exists and is wired, shipped in commit 969bb9da0 (release: 6.1.0). A real residual hole remained and is what this change closes.

already_present_evidence.model: native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/api/devices/simulation.rs: SIM_SLEW_DEG_PER_SEC / SIM_MIN_SLEW_SECS / SIM_FLIP_TRAVERSE_DEG, struct SimSlew, angular_separation_deg(), sim_slew_duration_secs(), interpolate_ra(), begin_sim_slew(), advance_sim_slew(), cancel_sim_slew()
already_present_evidence.wiring: ops/mount.rs: mount_slew + mount_slew_alt_az call begin_sim_slew; mount_sync/mount_park/mount_find_home/mount_stop/mount_abort call cancel_sim_slew; every simulator status read goes through sim_gate::read_mount_status which drove advance_sim_slew

residual_gap_found: advance_sim_slew() is interpolation, not a motor -- nothing runs it on a timer, and only the READ gate ran it. A command that arrived without a status read first therefore acted on the pointing as of the last poll. Consequences: (1) aborting a slew nobody had polled froze the mount on its EXACT START coordinates, the one position a real abort can never leave you in, so 'stopped part-way, pointing at neither end' was unreachable; (2) re-targeting mid-slew teleported the mount BACKWARDS to the abandoned slew's start, because begin_sim_slew reads 'from' out of the stale singleton.
why_it_matters: The pre-existing abort test asserted only 'did not arrive at the target', which is trivially true when the mount never moved at all. So the simulator passed in the pass-making direction: any caller that treats 'not slewing, still at the origin' as 'the slew never began, the pointing is still trustworthy' was never exercised against the state real hardware actually leaves.
fix: sim_gate.rs: extracted advance_mount_motion() (which keeps the existing sim_faults is_stalled('mount.slew') suppression) and called it from require_mount_connected() -- the write gate every mutating simulator mount op (slew, sync, park, find_home, stop, abort, set_tracking, move_axis) runs first -- as well as from read_mount_status().
tests_drive_the_wiring: All three drive the real DeviceManager (get_device_manager().mount_slew / mount_abort / mount_get_status) against a registered DriverType::Simulator mount. None calls the gate helper directly.

revert_proof.method: Removed the single line `advance_mount_motion().await;` from require_mount_connected(), rebuilt, reran.
revert_proof.result: 2 of 3 FAILED with the predicted symptom -- 'the mount reported RA 0.0000h -- it was aborted on its start coordinates' and 'the mount jumped back to RA 0.0002h, the start of the slew it had already abandoned'. Line restored; all 3 pass again.
revert_proof.third_test: a_stalled_mount_does_not_creep_forward_when_a_command_arrives passes either way by design -- it guards the is_stalled suppression inside advance_mount_motion, i.e. it fails against a WRONG version of this fix rather than against its absence.

caveats: SIM_SLEW_DEG_PER_SEC = 180.0 deg/s (simulation.rs:614) is 30-60x faster than any real GEM (3-6 deg/s). Every slew on the sky finishes in <= 1.0 s, or <= 2.0 s with a pier crossing. A UI or sequencer polling at ~1 Hz can therefore miss the entire slew, so slew-PROGRESS rendering is still only marginally exercisable. The existing comment justifies it (motion must complete inside a test budget). NOT CHANGED: simulation.rs is owned by another agent this session.

No settle phase. `slewing` drops to false the instant the interpolation reaches fraction 1.0. Real drivers hold Slewing true through a mechanical settle, and the app's own history includes a post-flip guiding-settle bug. Adding e.g. a SIM_SLEW_SETTLE_SECS tail inside SimSlew/advance_sim_slew would close it. NOT DONE: belongs in simulation.rs (another agent's file).

No 'refuse while moving' guard exists in the simulator itself -- mount_park / mount_sync / mount_slew all silently cancel an in-flight slew and succeed. Real ASCOM drivers raise InvalidOperationException for Park while Slewing. Closing that means editing ops/mount.rs (not this agent's file).
